description: Audit your own delimited data against a contract you declare, and get one pass/fail plus the exact row and clause of every breach. Checks types, required values, enums, numeric bounds, lengths, patterns, uniqueness, composite primary keys, null-rate ceilings, header drift and encoding damage in one pass. A pass means the audit was complete and nothing broke, so a file beyond the bounds reports incomplete rather than passing. Nothing is fetched: you supply the rows. Pay 120000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

allow_extra_columns.description: Defaults to true. Set false to report undeclared columns as violations rather than warnings.

enum.description: The complete set of permitted values, compared as exact text.

max.description: Inclusive upper bound, applied to values that read as numeric.

max_null_rate.description: Highest tolerable proportion of empty values, as a fraction. 0.02 means 2%.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound, applied to values that read as numeric.

name.description: Column name as it appears in the header row.

pattern.description: Pattern every non-empty value must match in full. A deliberately safe non-backtracking subset: literals with backslash escaping, dot, character classes with ranges and negation, the usual shorthands, and the ?, *, +, {n}, {n,} and {n,m} quantifiers. Groups, alternation, backreferences and lookaround are refused by name, which is what makes a catastrophic pattern impossible rather than merely unlikely. Values longer than 256 characters report as not evaluated rather than as a pass.

required.description: When true, an empty value in this column is a violation.

type.description: Defaults to string. Recognition is strict and locale-free: no thousands separators, and dates must be ISO-8601.

unique.description: When true, a repeated value is reported with the row it first appeared on.

primary_key.description: One or more declared column names forming a composite key checked for duplicates.

require_column_order.description: Defaults to false. Set true to report a reordered header as a violation.

csv.description: Delimited text including a header row, at most 262144 bytes. RFC 4180 quoting is honoured.

delimiter.description: Single field separator. Defaults to a comma; a tab or semicolon is accepted.

name: tabular_contract_audit

column_profiles.description: Per column: declared and dominant inferred type, counts per inferred type, null count and rate, distinct count, numeric and length extremes.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means some of the data was not seen, which is a different problem from data that is wrong.

encoding.description: Byte order mark, U+FFFD replacement characters, CRLF and mixed line endings.

header.description: Observed and declared column names, with missing, unexpected, duplicated and whether the order changed.

not_examined.description: Named reasons anything was left unexamined: rows beyond the bound, cells too long, values beyond pattern or numeric range, or violations found but not listed.

passed.description: The single field to branch on. True only when the audit was complete and nothing it examined broke the contract, so a file larger than the row bound can never report a pass.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

row_count.description: Data rows audited, excluding the header.

supplied_row_count.description: Data rows supplied. Higher than row_count when the row bound was reached.

violation_count.description: The true total, including any beyond the listing bound.

violations.description: Every breach, naming the row and the clause it broke.

row.description: 1-based and counting the header row, so it matches a text editor.

violations_by_code.description: Counts per violation code, for triage without reading the list.

title: Tabular Contract Audit
